answer: A harbour wharf only lets a ship dock after it shows a lantern signal that matches a costly, verifiable record: likewise, an agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake and complete attested work before it earns. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand stakes plus a thousand proofs, while a single honest agent pays once. If an identity cheats, its stake is slashed and its delta of reputation — the change from trusted to penalised — is published, so Sybils cannot simply reappear free under a new name.
